ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation was driver-side on a no-show claim, so NS-0 routes the fee's validity entirely into NS-1, whose elements (i)–(iii) must all hold before the $6.61 may be kept [F4][F7][NS-0]. Arrival confirmation is settled: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 13:02:35, 39 m from the pickup, satisfying NS-1(i) and (ii) [F6][NS-1].

The wait element NS-1(iii) fails. The clause requires continuous waiting at the pickup for more than 3 minutes — at least 3:01 — after the arrival confirmation, and time spent nearby before the tap is expressly not counted [F6][NS-1]. The trace measures 175 s (2 min 55 s) continuously inside 200 m after the 13:02:35 tap, below the 180 s threshold [F6]. The earlier platform-recorded arrival at 13:01:00 and the 4 min 30 s cumulative in-radius time include pre-tap time and cannot repair the shortfall [F2][F5]. The driver's stationary spell ran 13:02:15–13:05:30, but its first 20 seconds precede the tap [F3].

Because (iii) is unmet, NS-2 applies and the $6.61 must be refunded in full [F4][F7][NS-2]. The driver's post-hoc statement that he waited more than 3 minutes is a statement contradicted by the system records, which prevail [F12][NS-1]. The NS-2 account flag does not attach: the tap was made at 39 m, inside the radius, so there was no fake confirmation [F6][NS-2]. The driver's profile (1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days) cannot decide this case and does not by itself reach RD-6, which is a route-deviation clause in any event [F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint [F9][F10][F12]. They contain only an arrival notice, a cancellation notice and a factual account; nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses or alleges dangerous driving, so safety_concern is "none" [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1].

Evidence: the chat record is complete and fully timestamped, and the GPS trace covers the wait from the arrival confirmation to cancellation with no gap, so the elements NS-1(iii) turns on are settled and evidence_status is "sufficient" [F2][F6][F11][NS-1].

rejected_claims.reason: NS-1(iii) counts only continuous waiting inside the pickup radius after the arrival confirmation [F6]; the 4 min 30 s cumulative and the 3 min 15 s stationary spell both begin before the 13:02:35 tap (the stationary spell starts 13:02:15), and the measured post-tap in-radius time is only 2 min 55 s, below the 3:01 minimum [F2][F3][F6][NS-1].

The absence of a rider reply in the two-message chat shows only that the rider did not answer; it does not establish the length of the driver's in-radius wait after his arrival tap, which the GPS record puts at 2 min 55 s [F9][F10][F11][F6][NS-1].

NS-0 only channels a driver-side no-show cancellation into NS-1, and NS-1 makes the fee conditional on all of (i)–(iii); with (iii) unmet the fee is not provided for and NS-2 requires its full refund [F4][F7][F6][NS-0][NS-1][NS-2].

The rider's 'one minute' account carries no weight, but the system records themselves defeat the fee: measured from the arrival tap as NS-1(iii) prescribes, the in-radius wait was 2 min 55 s, short of 3:01 [F2][F3][F6][NS-1].

That no safety incident or GPS hole appears goes only to the evidentiary completeness of the wait; it does not cure the failed NS-1(iii) wait element, and the fee still falls under NS-2 [F5][F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2].

The driver's profile (2 disputes, 1 upheld no-show in 90 days) cannot decide this case or ground an account flag: profile facts never decide alone, NS-2's flag requires a tap made while GPS showed the driver outside the radius (here the tap was at 39 m, inside), and RD-6 concerns route-deviation repeats, not this no-show case [F17][F6][NS-2][RD-6]. The refund rests on the failed NS-1(iii), not on the profile.

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.
